back_translation: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Which way has your beloved turned? We will help you seek him.
My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.
I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
My darling, you are as beautiful as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem, as awe-inspiring as an army with banners.
Turn your eyes away from me, for they make my heart tremble. Your hair is like a flock of goats flowing down from Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; every one has its twin, and not one of them is missing.
Your temple behind your veil is like a split pomegranate.
There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and young women beyond counting,

but my dove, my flawless one, is one and only. She is the only one of her mother, the pure darling of the one who bore her. The young women saw her and blessed her; the queens and the concubines praised her.
Who is this who shines forth like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, radiant as the sun, awe-inspiring as an army with banners?
I went down to the walnut grove to look at the budding trees of the valley, to see whether the vines had blossomed and the pomegranates were in flower.
Before I knew it, my heart had set me among the chariots of my noble people.
